text:
Most people are using Grok Bot to book dinner reservations. We’re using it to run 7 business workflows that touch AEO, organic social, recruiting, sales, and code.

I’ve included the links for each of these below.

Autonomous Engine Optimization

This bot finds SEO and AEO opportunities, then uses ClickFlow to create drafts.

It can surface 40 candidates per week. We pick 20, and WordPress keeps them in draft until approval.

It also measures whether the content produces leads. Traffic is nice, but leads are what the business cares about.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/Jyx1Lg-VzYgyjDc-y-GQi 

Trial Reels

This bot pulled nine Reel candidates from one YouTube video.

The first drafts found good moments and wrote solid titles. The edits still needed captions, overlays, and tighter cuts.

That’s normal. Bots need feedback before they become reliable.

Now it can test multiple versions against non-followers. If one gets 10,000 views while the others get 100, we know which idea deserves another iteration.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/HktaB2ID5y5djGCrRAxvf

Short-Form Scaler

This bot uses the @Overlap_AI API to find clips inside webinars, podcasts, and long-form videos.

The goal is to produce at least four candidates each day.
A human picks the winners before anything gets published. Once the workflow works consistently, someone on the social team can manage it.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/NA1zDLMoKJZVcjl3mZ2tT

Sponsorship Deal Desk

This bot handles the first response when a sponsor reaches out.

It can reply within 60 seconds with a minimum price of $15,000 or $25,000, depending on the opportunity.

Most bots aren’t allowed to send anything automatically. This one can because the message, pricing rules, and authority are narrowly defined.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/bFrGNsUsXpsIfnCIUEvKy

Outreach

This bot supports outreach through tools like HeyReach and LinkedIn Sales Navigator/Recruiter.

It finds prospects, checks whether they match our criteria, and prepares a limited number of messages.

There are daily caps. If the bot can’t find enough qualified people, it doesn’t lower the bar to hit a quota.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/wexM_NUvEByvLwrnTR_F3

Talent Bot

The Talent bot reviews applicants across our recruiting systems.

It asks candidates how much of their work is done with AI, which tools they use every day, and what they’ve built.

It also asks which old workflows they’ve stopped using.
Someone who already thinks this way can become an agent manager much faster than someone who needs to unlearn how they work.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/P2cMMcajyHuHZ4OsZOWfe

Pre-Call Intelligence

This bot prepares the team before an important meeting.

It reviews previous conversations and explains what the other party cares about.

Before one private equity meeting, it warned the team to focus on private equity instead of talking about VCs like Sequoia or Andreessen Horowitz.

Small detail. Big difference in the room.

Link: https://x.ai/bot/yQRbVJ7aZL2DyPAWulXn7

Each bot has one job.

Anything sensitive stops for human review. Caps keep the volume sane, and evals decide whether the work is good enough.

If a bot keeps missing, it gets parked.

The bottleneck is moving from doing the work to managing the agents that do it.

Everyone on our team will need to get good at that.

Anything you would add?
